summary: Tenant experiences intermittent unpinning during SLO-driven canary throttle leading to fallback to older variant
description:
Issue summary: GreenPlan (dedicated customer) reports intermittent model unpinning for tenant 'greenplan-prod' during a scheduled canary that uses an SLO-driven throttle. The unpinning results in traffic falling back to an older, higher-latency variant and occasional 5xx error bursts.

Impact: Multiple customer-facing endpoints serving critical analytics pipelines see increased 95th and 99th percentile latencies and ~1.8% error rate spike for 20-40 minute windows during canary throttle events. Business impact: delayed reports and one customer SLA alert triggered.

Environment: production (us-east), tenant: greenplan-prod, dedicated pool id: dp-42, canary config: weight 5%, SLO throttle enabled (latency target 250ms).

Observed behavior: During an autoscaler-triggered SLO throttle (latency breach), orchestrator moves a subset of canary cohort to a protected low-throughput bucket. Shortly after, edge logs show session affinity tokens for the tenant are removed or replaced and requests are routed to an older variant (llama2-13b-redwood-v1) instead of the pinned quantized variant. Some requests then time out and return 5xx.

Expected behavior: SLO-driven throttling should reduce throughput but preserve tenant-level model pinning and not evict affinity leases. Fallback routing should only occur after explicit model health or capacity signals, not as a side-effect of throttle-induced cohort migration.

Steps to reproduce: see steps_to_reproduce field.

Attachments: partial logs, sample request IDs, control-plane snapshot links included below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On prod us-east, schedule a canary rollout for model llama2-13b-quantized-v1 with weight 5% and SLO enforcement on latency target 250ms.
2) Generate load that increases tail latency above the SLO (synthetic traffic at 1.5x peak for 10-20 minutes).
3) Observe orchestrator perform SLO throttle and shift canary cohort into low-throughput bucket; monitor control-plane snapshots for dp-42 cohort placement.
4) Inspect edge-proxy logs for tenant greenplan-prod session affinity token churn and routing decisions for the same session IDs (should see variant flip to llama2-13b-redwood-v1).
5) Verify downstream responses: increased latency and occasional 5xx errors for affected requests.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 15:00 — Support (Maya): validated customer timeline and collected request IDs and control-plane snapshot references.
2026-03-12 15:30 — SRE (Diego): reproduced cohort migration by triggering SLO throttle in staging and observed edge affinity eviction during orchestrator snapshot apply.

2026-03-12 16:10 — Hypothesis A: orchestrator's cohort migration path triggers a full affinity reconciliation that unintentionally clears tenant pin metadata on the edge if the migration uses in-place reshard semantics.
2026-03-12 16:35 — Hypothesis B: lease TTL mismatch between control-plane commit and edge-side cache causes transient eviction when throttle causes rapid cohort reassignments.

2026-03-12 17:05 — Observed that fallback routing policy treats low_throughput bucket as incompatible with quantized runtime (quantized variant not prewarmed in low_throughput), so routing falls back to older non-quantized variant.

2026-03-12 17:40 — Preliminary root-cause candidate: combined effect of (1) affinity eviction during orchestrator cohort resync, and (2) bucket-level runtime mismatch causing automatic model-variant fallback.
workaround: Applied temporary tenant-level static pin via control-plane override (force model=llama2-13b-quantized-v1 for greenplan-prod) and disabled SLO-driven cohort throttle for dp-42. This stabilized routing within 5 minutes and reduced 5xxs. Note: static pin is an emergency setting and requires manual revert after fix.
resolution: Mitigation in progress. Engineering to implement two changes: (A) make orchestrator cohort migration a lease-friendly operation that preserves tenant affinity tokens; (B) add a runtime-compatibility check before treating a bucket as 'incompatible' fallback to avoid silent variant swap. ETA for deploy to staging: 2026-03-18. Patch PR referenced in comments.

2026-03-12 16:20 Priya Rao (Infra): Confirmed affinity eviction occurs during applySnapshot() path in orchestrator; suspect ordering between snapshot commit and edge notification is inverted under throttle. Filed upstream PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/582.

2026-03-12 17:50 Maya Kline (Support): Applied emergency static pin override and disabled SLO throttle for dp-42 per customer's permission. Customer acknowledged temporary fix; monitoring for 30 minutes stable.

follow_up_actions: 1) Deploy orchestrator patch that preserves edge affinity tokens during cohort migration (PR #582).
2) Add compatibility prewarm step for low_throughput buckets to avoid variant fallback when a tenant is pinned to quantized runtime.
3) Add guard in control-plane: do not trigger SLO throttle that moves cohorts if static tenant pin override is present.
4) Postmortem and runbook update: document this class of interaction between SLO-throttle, cohort migration, and model-variant compatibility.
